findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how `legacy_impact_plan`, `classify`, and `RULES` become importable from `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/` (e.g., relocate them into an importable module under `src/` and cite the new path, or add `docs/calibration/` to the path via a documented shim), since `docs/calibration/` has no `__init__.py` and is not on the import path.
evidence: `legacy_impact_plan` at docs/calibration/plan_v5_rescore.py:162; `classify` at :127; `RULES` at :124 — all module-level in a script under docs/
`list_directory docs/calibration` shows no `__init__.py` — the directory is not a package and is not on sys.path for a src/ module
Scope lists only new files under `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/` and generated docs; no step relocates or makes `docs/calibration/plan_v5_rescore.py` importable
findings.finding: The plan asserts AC2's replay uses `legacy_impact_plan` '(imported)' and reuses `classify`/`RULES` — but these live in `docs/calibration/plan_v5_rescore.py`, a standalone script under a directory with no `__init__.py` and not on the Python import path, so they are not importable from the new `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/` package as the plan's wording ('imported') presupposes.
findings.location: Context: 'Plan-v4->v5 baseline' paragraph ('AC2's replay uses `legacy_impact_plan` (imported)'); Approach bullet 'Plan-v4->v5 replay (AC2): `classify`/`RULES`...`legacy_impact_plan`'; AC2
scenarios: Author writes `from docs.calibration.plan_v5_rescore import legacy_impact_plan, classify, RULES` in tier0.py and it fails at import time (docs/ is not a package)
AC2 cannot run because the pre-v5 baseline function is unreachable from the new package
findings.suggested_fix: Relocate `legacy_impact_plan`/`classify`/`RULES` (or thin re-exports) into an importable module under `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/` (e.g. `candidates/plan_v5_baseline.py`) and have both the docs script and tier0.py import from there, then update AC2/Context to cite that path.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm at least one non-'current' candidate (an overlay experiment) is intended in the near-term done-definition, or justify the CANDIDATES registry as the deliberate extension surface for Tier-0 threshold sweeps rather than premature abstraction.
evidence: Only 'current' is named as a concrete candidate at build time ("'current' is built-in with an empty overlay and default impact_fn")

The overlay/impact_fn override mechanism directly serves the stated done-definition (candidate-vs-live-baseline diffing is Tier-0's actual purpose), so YAGNI is arguably satisfied — hence a confirmation, not an assertion
findings.finding: The CANDIDATES registry (dict[str, Candidate]) plus the Candidate dataclass (overlay + impact_fn) is introduced with a single built-in member ('current', empty overlay, default impact_fn) — a Rule-of-Three concern for the registry abstraction.
findings.location: Approach / Context: "Resolved via .../candidates/__init__.py's CANDIDATES: dict[str, Candidate]"
scenarios: If no experimental candidate is ever registered beyond 'current', the registry indirection (KeyError->error listing, dict lookup) is scaffolding around a single identity-check candidate

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the candidate's mirrored threshold_for applies the overlay as a per-criterion OVERRIDE and then re-runs _criteria.threshold_for's MIN-threshold / ANY-blocking-posture aggregation across ALL of a finding's criteria (overlaid + live-resolved), and add a unit test with a multi-criterion finding where the overlaid criterion is not the aggregation winner.
evidence: _criteria.threshold_for computes block_threshold = MIN over the criteria's thresholds and blocking = ANY criterion blocking (src/rebar/llm/criteria/model.py:55,68-81)
Candidate.overlay is 'dict[str, tuple[float, bool]] per-criterion threshold/posture override' — an override keyed per criterion, not per finding

A plan-review finding may carry multiple criteria (pass3_over_findings iterates f.get('criteria', []) as a list); an overlay that touches one criterion must still be combined (min/any) with the OTHER criteria's live-resolved (block_threshold, blocking) or the mirrored resolver diverges from orchestrator behavior
Candidate-vs-live-baseline flips are the plan's stated primary signal, so a resolver aggregation bug corrupts the headline metric silently
findings.finding: The candidate mirror's per-criterion overlay resolution does not specify how a partial overlay (overriding only SOME of a multi-criterion finding's criteria) combines with the live-resolved thresholds of the finding's remaining criteria; _criteria.threshold_for aggregates via MIN-threshold and ANY-blocking-posture, so a whole-finding replacement would mis-resolve and silently mis-count candidate-induced flips.
findings.location: Approach / Context — 'The candidate's threshold_for mirrors _threshold_for's logic resolved against the overlay'
scenarios: An overlay lowers criterion X's threshold; a finding cites {X, Y} where Y (live) is more aggressive — mirror must keep Y's lower threshold (MIN), not X's overlaid value
An overlay sets X non-blocking; a finding cites {X, Y} where Y is blocking — mirror must stay blocking (ANY)
findings.suggested_fix: Build the candidate resolver by taking crit_by_id, replacing overridden criteria's block_threshold/default_posture entries with the overlay values, then delegating to the SAME _criteria.threshold_for(..., gate='plan_review') (plus the prerequisite-consistency short-circuit and execution_review bump) so the min/any aggregation is shared verbatim rather than re-implemented.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Qualify the `orchestrator.py` and `sidecar.py` citations with their full `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/` path to disambiguate them from the same-named `review_kernel.pass3_over_findings`.
evidence: `orchestrator.py:662-711` and `sidecar.py:702-703` cited without a directory; the files resolve to `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py` (pass3_over_findings at line 662) and `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py` (block_threshold/blocking_enabled at lines 702-703)
review_kernel/ contains only __init__.py, coach.py, decide.py, discovery.py, discovery_shadow.py, telemetry.py, verify.py, verify_models.py — no orchestrator.py or sidecar.py
A second `review_kernel/decide.py:753 def pass3_over_findings` exists distinct from `plan_review/orchestrator.py:662 def pass3_over_findings`
findings.finding: The plan cites `orchestrator.py:662-711` and `sidecar.py:702-703` with bare filenames and no directory prefix; both actually live in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/`, not `review_kernel/` where the co-cited `decide.py` lives. Because a DISTINCT `review_kernel.pass3_over_findings` also exists (the plan itself contrasts it with `orchestrator.pass3_over_findings` as 'the REAL LIVE plan-review path'), the un-prefixed locators invite a reader to look in `review_kernel/` and either fail to find the file or conflate the two same-named functions.
scenarios: An implementer greps review_kernel/ for orchestrator.py and finds nothing, or wires the candidate mirror against review_kernel.pass3_over_findings instead of the live orchestrator path

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the candidate's threshold_for stays in lockstep with orchestrator._threshold_for's special-case/bump logic (e.g. factor the special-case+bump into a shared helper both call, or add a test asserting the mirror matches _threshold_for on the prerequisite-consistency and execution_review branches for an empty overlay).
evidence: orchestrator.py:681-689 `_threshold_for` is a private closure over crit_by_id/execution_review that hardcodes `if 'prerequisite-consistency' in set(criteria): return 0.60, True` and `if execution_review and blocking_enabled: block_threshold = max(block_threshold, 0.80)`
The plan requires the candidate resolver to apply the SAME special-case + bump but resolved against the overlay — a hand-copied mirror, not a shared function
A2 harness self-check asserts replayed-stored==stored but nothing pins the candidate mirror to the live _threshold_for behaviour for the special-case/bump branches
findings.finding: The candidate's threshold_for is specified only as 'mirrors _threshold_for's logic resolved against the overlay', which duplicates production threshold-resolution logic (the prerequisite-consistency->(0.60,True) special case and the execution_review>=0.80 bump) that can drift out of sync with the orchestrator.
findings.location: Approach / Context: "The candidate's threshold_for mirrors _threshold_for's logic resolved against the overlay"
scenarios: A future change to the prerequisite-consistency threshold or the execution-review bump in orchestrator._threshold_for is not reflected in the mirrored candidate resolver, so candidate-vs-live-baseline flips are attributed to the overlay when they are actually a stale mirror
findings.suggested_fix: Extract the prerequisite-consistency special case and execution_review bump into a small shared helper (parameterised by the resolved (block_threshold, blocking_enabled)) that both orchestrator._threshold_for and the candidate resolver call, so the overlay only changes the base resolution and the special-case/bump cannot drift.
